previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of polysubstance abuse, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, systolic heart failure, and COPD, was admitted with chest pain and rapid atrial fibrillation after being found unconscious outside in cold weather. He had missed his metoprolol, leading to tachycardia, which resolved with IV diltiazem and oral medication restart. He was diagnosed with frostbite in both feet due to prolonged cold exposure, presenting with discolored, numb, and painful toes. His treatment included pain management with oxycodone and gabapentin, pentoxifylline for circulation, and supportive care with warming, elevation, and wound protection. Lab abnormalities including leukocytosis, elevated lactate, and anion gap metabolic acidosis resolved with supportive care. He remained hemodynamically stable, with no evidence of acute myocardial infarction or infection. He was discharged to extended care with plans for podiatry follow-up, medication continuation, and foot care instructions.

and cough initially productive of white, later yellow, sputum. 
He observed that cough frequently followed cigarette smoking and 
reduced tobacco use from 1 pack per day to 0.5 pack per day, 
without significant relief. He also self-uptitrated fluticasone 
inhaler use, with limited symptomatic improvement. Over the same 
period, he describes persistence of his chronic chest pain 
syndrome, specifically sharp intermittent left upper chest pain, 
radiating occasionally to the ipsilateral shoulder, occurring at 
rest, not worsened reliably by exertion and unassociated with 
nausea or diaphoresis. This chest pain syndrome is distinct from 
his anginal equivalent, which is crushing. At baseline, he 
states that he is able to walk at least blocks without dyspnea, 
with activity limited by toe amputations rather than true 
exercise intolerance. He endorses a 20-lb unintentional weight 
loss over the past ___ months without recent regain, 
intermittent palpitations increased by activity, stable 4-pillow 
orthopnea that he attributes to personal preference, and 
abdominal distention that has since resolved, but denies recent 
fevers, chills, sweats, lightheadedness, pleuritic chest pain, 
hemoptysis, peripheral edema, myalgias, or clear sick contacts, 
noting, however, that many of his friends are homeless and could 
have been ill. He endorses compliance with all of his 
medications and denies heroin and cocaine use ""for years.""  
  
He was evaluated initially in the ED on ___ for exertional 
dyspnea and chest pain, cough, and wheeze felt to be most 
consistent with a COPD exacerbation, for which he received a 
4-day prednisone burst and refills of his home COPD and other 
medications. He was seen in primary care clinic in follow-up on 
___, by which time his symptoms had improved mostly, but not 
entirely. Since that time, he has experienced recrudescence of 
his symptoms, accelerated perhaps over the past few days, 
prompting him to represent to the ED.  
   
Of note, he has had multiple admissions for similar symptoms, 
most recently from ___, when he was noted to be in rapid 
atrial fibrillation in the setting of missed metoprolol doses 
and also managed conservatively for ___ bite. Prior to that 
time, he was hospitalized from ___ for dyspnea and 
palpitations attributed to decompensated systolic heart failure, 
rapid atrial fibrillation, COPD exacerbation, and resolving 
multifocal pneumonia from a preceding admission, prompting 
diuresis, rate control, treatment with a 6-day prednisone burst, 
and completion of a 7-day course of levofloxacin. He also 
received methadone for heroin withdrawal, with plan for referral 
to a ___ clinic.
     
In the ED, initial vital signs were as follows: 96.5, ___, 32, 98% RA. He triggered on arrival for rapid atrial 
fibrillation. Admission labs were notable for Wbc of 11.5 (70.8% 
PMNs), essentially unremarkable CBC and Chem7, normal 
coagulation panel, normal lipase, TnT of 0.02, lactate of 1.9, 
and proBNP of 3967. Blood culture was obtained. EKG was felt to 
be consistent with rapid atrial fibrillation with nonspecific ST 
changes unchanged from prior. Portable CXR was interpreted as 
demonstrating left-sided opacity and mild pulmonary edema, but 
prelimary report was negative for acute cardiopulmonary process, 
including focal infiltrate or pulmonary edema. For heart rate 
peaking at 145, he received metoprolol tartrate 5mg IV followed 
by metoprolol tartrate 25mg PO, with improvement in heart rate 
to 100s. He also received vancomycin 1g IV, ceftriaxone 1g IV, 
azithromycin 500mg IV, ipratropium nebs, and 
oxycodone/acetaminophen 5mg/325mg x1 prior to admission. IV 
fluids were deferred, given concern for volume overload, as were 
systemic glucocorticoids. Vital signs prior to transfer were as 
follows: 98.6, 107, 113/75, 23, 98% RA.  
   
On the floor, he is mildly short of breath upright in bed and 
continues to feel wheezy, but improved following nebulizer 
treatment in the ED. He denies chest pain, last experienced on 
the afternoon of admission, or palpitations.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with coronary artery disease status post 
multiple PCIs, systolic heart failure (LVEF ___ in ___, 
atrial fibrillation not on systemic anticoagulation, COPD, and 
polysubstance misuse (narcotics, cocaine, tobacco) who presents 
with shortness of breath, most likley due to COPD exacerbation.  
 
   
# COPD exacerbation: Patient presented with shortness of breath 
and dyspnea on exertion, with wheeze appreciated on exam, 
respiratory rate of 32, and requiring 2L O2 in the ED. The 
etiology of this SOB was thought to be due to a COPD 
exacerbation precipitated by viral bronchitis, so he was treated 
with 40mg prednisone and ipraproium nebs. Initially, there was 
concern for focal opacity on CXR, so patient received 
broad-spectrum antibiotics in the ED (vancomycin 1g IV, 
ceftriaxone 1g IV, azithromycin 500mg IV), but final radiology 
read negative for focal opacity and he had no other infectious 
symptoms so broad spectrum coverage DCd. The patient was 
continued on prednisone 40mg daily x 5 days and azithromycin 
250mg daily. Given poor COPD control at home, fluticasone was 
discontinued and started on Advair 500/50 bid. At time of 
discharge, the patient was breathing comfortably on room air 
with O2 sats in the high ___.  
      
# Atrial fibrillation: Chronic Afib, CHADS score of 2 but not on 
systemic anticoagulation bc of social instability. Admitted with 
atrial fibrillation with RVR to 140s, improved to 100s after 
administration of metoprolol tartrate 5mg IV followed by 
metoprolol tartrate 25mg PO. The patient was continued on 
metoprolol tartrate 75mg TID during this admission, and 
restarted on home dose metoprolol succinate 200 PO QD at time of 
discharge.
      
# Leukocytosis: Patient noted to have leukocytosis to 11.5K on 
admission with PMN predominance on admission, which improved to 
9K on day of discharge. Leukocytosis likley in the setting of 
phsysiologic stress. No evidence of PNA given negative CXR, 
afebrile, no other systemic signs of infection, blood cultures 
from ___ pending.  
      
# Systolic heart failure: Patient has sCHF EF ___. 
proBNP elevated to 3967 at time of admisison, which is near his 
baseline. His weight is decreased from last available in ___ 
He reported mild PND and orthopnea but reported, unchanged from 
baseline. On exam, he did not appear volume overloaded and CXR 
without pulmonary  edema. During this admission, we continued 
home furosemide 60mg PO QD, lisinopril, and metoprolol.
  
# Coronary artery disease: The patient reports intermittent 
chest pain at rest and with activity, which he reports is 
different from the crushing anginal chest pain that he has 
experienced in the past. EKG on ___trial 
fibrillation with nonspecific ST changes unchanged from prior; 
cardiac enzymes negative for acute coronary syndrome. Patient 
strongly denied cocaine use, but urine toxicology screen 
positive for cocaine. Continued home aspirin, clopidogrel, 
atorvastatin, metoprolol, and lisinopril. At time of discharge, 
patient denied chest pain or pressure.  
  
# Polysubstance misuse: Patient has a history of misusing 
multiple substances, including narcotics, cocaine, and tobacco. 
Patient strongly denied cocaine use, but urine toxicology screen 
positive for cocaine. Continued home thiamine, folate, 
multivitamin, and nicotine patch.  
  
# Hypertension: Stable, chronic. Continued home lisinopril and 
metoprolol as above. 
   
# Hyperlipidemia: Stable, chronic. Continued home atorvastatin.  

  
# Anxiety: Stable, chronic. Continued home bupropion and 
clonazepam.  
  
# h/o toe frostbite: Stable, chronic. No evidence of infection. 
Continued home oxycodone/acetaminophen and gabapentin.
  
Transitional Issues:
- Full Code
- Inhaled Fluticasone changed to Advair due to multiple 
presentations for COPD exacerbations
- Prednisone and Azithromycin for 5 day course
- UTox positive for cocaine. Patient extensively counseled to 
avoid cocaine use especially while on Metoprolol. Since he has 
been on this medication for years and has been using cocaine for 
years, Metoprolol was not changed but should be discussed a 
combined alpha-beta antagonist in the outpatient setting.
